fabrics.name: Ankara
fabrics.spotlight: Bold, wax-printed cotton worn across West Africa. In Nigeria it is everywhere: everyday styles, office Fridays, aso-ebi and party looks. Its history runs through Dutch and West African trade, but Nigerians made it their own.

fabrics.name: Aso-oke (Sanyan)
fabrics.spotlight: Hand-woven on narrow looms by Yoruba weavers, then sewn together from strips. Sanyan, the classic beige, is traditionally woven from wild silk and considered one of the most prestigious types.

fabrics.name: Aso-oke (Alaari)
fabrics.spotlight: Alaari is the rich red aso-oke, one of the three classic types alongside sanyan and etu. A statement at any Yoruba celebration.

fabrics.name: Aso-oke (Etu)
fabrics.spotlight: Etu is the deep indigo aso-oke, often with fine stripes. Dignified, elegant, and loved by elders.

fabrics.name: Adire (Eleko)
fabrics.spotlight: Indigo resist-dyed cloth strongly associated with Abeokuta. In adire eleko, patterns are painted or stencilled with a starch paste before dyeing, leaving pale designs on deep blue.

fabrics.name: Adire (Oniko)
fabrics.spotlight: Tie-resist adire: cloth is tied or bound before dyeing, creating circles and ripples. The basis of the in-game Adire Studio.

fabrics.name: George
fabrics.spotlight: Heavy, often richly embroidered wrapper fabric, loved for Igbo and Niger Delta ceremonies. Worn as double wrappers with blouses, coral beads and a matching head tie.

fabrics.name: Lace
fabrics.spotlight: From cord lace to beaded French lace, lace is an after-party essential. Nigerians are among the world's biggest lace buyers.

fabrics.name: Brocade (Shadda)
fabrics.spotlight: Stiff, shiny damask-woven cloth. Popular for babban riga and agbada, often heavily embroidered.

fabrics.name: Atiku
fabrics.spotlight: Soft, fine men's fabric for kaftans and senator styles. Clean, sharp, and always appropriate.

fabrics.name: Akwete
fabrics.spotlight: Hand-woven cloth from Akwete in Abia State, traditionally made by Igbo women weavers, known for intricate geometric motifs.

fabrics.name: Kano Indigo
fabrics.spotlight: Deep indigo cloth from Kano's centuries-old Kofar Mata dye pits. Unlocks in the Kano Gold chapter.
